blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(4\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Is part mein answer key ne sin ka sign ghalat liya hai, is liye quadrant wala qadam bohat dhyan se dekhiye.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r = 4\), \(\theta = \frac{5\pi}{3}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): z ko \(x + iy\) (rectangular form) mein likhna.
Method (tareeqa): \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\). Yeh is liye lagta hai ke cos 'daayein-baayein' ka hissa aur sin 'upar-neeche' ka hissa deta hai.

Angle badlein aur quadrant pehchanein
\[\dfrac{5\pi}{3} = 5 \times 60^{\circ} = 300^{\circ}\]
\(300^{\circ}\) chauthay (fourth) quadrant mein hai (\(270^{\circ}\) aur \(360^{\circ}\) ke darmiyan); reference angle \(360^{\circ} - 300^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}\).
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{3} = 60^{\circ}\), to \(\frac{5\pi}{3} = 300^{\circ}\). Fourth quadrant mein cos positive aur sin negative hota hai. Yaad rakhiye: first quadrant mein sab positive, second mein sirf sin positive, third mein sirf tan positive (cos aur sin dono negative), fourth mein sirf cos positive.

cos aur sin ki values
\[\cos 300^{\circ} = \cos 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\sin 300^{\circ} = -\sin 60^{\circ} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Kyun: size (value) reference angle \(60^{\circ}\) se aata hai, aur sign quadrant se.
Dhyan dein: \(\sin 300^{\circ}\) negative hai. Agar yeh minus bhool gaye to jawab \(2 + 2\sqrt{3}i\) ban jayega, jo answer key ki ghalti hai.

r se zarb dein
\[z = 4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 4\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)i\]
\[z = 2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta = 4 \times \frac{1}{2} = 2\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta = 4 \times \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -2\sqrt{3}\).

Tasdeeq (check):
Jawab ka modulus wapas r hona chahiye:
\[|z|^{2} = 2^{2} + (2\sqrt{3})^{2} = 4 + 12 = 16\]
is liye \(|z| = 4 = r\). Aur point \((2, -2\sqrt{3})\) fourth quadrant mein hai, jaisa angle keh raha tha. Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(z = 2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i \approx 2 - 3.46i\): yeh point fourth quadrant mein, O se 4 units door hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(2 + 2\sqrt{3}i\) deti hai. \(\frac{5\pi}{3} = 300^{\circ}\) fourth quadrant mein hai jahan sin negative hota hai, is liye sahi jawab \(2 - 2\sqrt{3}i\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(\frac{3}{2}\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Yahan angle third quadrant mein hai, jahan cos aur sin dono negative hote hain; answer key ne yahan values aur signs dono ulat diye hain.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r = \frac{3}{2}\), \(\theta = \frac{7\pi}{6}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): z ko \(x + iy\) (rectangular form) mein likhna.
Method (tareeqa): \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\). Yeh is liye lagta hai ke cos 'daayein-baayein' ka hissa aur sin 'upar-neeche' ka hissa deta hai.

Angle badlein aur quadrant pehchanein
\[\dfrac{7\pi}{6} = 7 \times 30^{\circ} = 210^{\circ}\]
Teesra (third) quadrant, reference angle \(210^{\circ} - 180^{\circ} = 30^{\circ}\).
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{6} = 30^{\circ}\), to \(\frac{7\pi}{6} = 210^{\circ}\), jo \(180^{\circ}\) se thora aage hai. Third quadrant mein cos aur sin dono negative hain.

cos aur sin ki values
\[\cos 210^{\circ} = -\cos 30^{\circ} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[\sin 210^{\circ} = -\sin 30^{\circ} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: values \(30^{\circ}\) se: \(\cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\); signs quadrant se, dono minus.
Dhyan dein: \(30^{\circ}\) ka cos \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) hai, \(\frac{1}{2}\) nahi. Cos aur sin ki values aapas mein ulat dena aam ghalti hai.

r se zarb dein
\[z = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + \dfrac{3}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)i\]
\[z = -\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4} - \dfrac{3}{4}i\]
Kyun: dono parts ko \(r = \frac{3}{2}\) se zarb diya; fractions mein upar upar se aur neeche neeche se zarb hota hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[|z|^{2} = \dfrac{27}{16} + \dfrac{9}{16} = \dfrac{36}{16}\]
is liye \(|z| = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2} = r\). Dono parts negative hain, yani point third quadrant mein hai. Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(z = -\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4} - \frac{3}{4}i \approx -1.30 - 0.75i\): third quadrant mein, O se 1.5 units door.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(-\frac{3}{4} + \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}i\) deti hai. Third quadrant mein cos aur sin dono negative hain, aur \(|\cos 210^{\circ}| = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(|\sin 210^{\circ}| = \frac{1}{2}\). Sahi jawab \(-\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4} - \frac{3}{4}i\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(|z| = 7,\ \arg(z) = \frac{23\pi}{12}\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Yahan \(15^{\circ}\) wala angle aata hai jo seedha standard angle nahi, lekin \(45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}\) se is ki exact values nikal sakti hain.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r = |z| = 7\), \(\theta = \arg(z) = \frac{23\pi}{12}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): z ko \(x + iy\) (rectangular form) mein likhna.
Method (tareeqa): \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\). Yeh is liye lagta hai ke cos 'daayein-baayein' ka hissa aur sin 'upar-neeche' ka hissa deta hai.

Angle badlein aur quadrant pehchanein
\[\dfrac{23\pi}{12} = 23 \times 15^{\circ} = 345^{\circ}\]
Chautha (fourth) quadrant, reference angle \(360^{\circ} - 345^{\circ} = 15^{\circ}\).
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{12} = \frac{180^{\circ}}{12} = 15^{\circ}\). \(345^{\circ}\) poore chakkar se sirf \(15^{\circ}\) kam hai, yani point positive x-axis ke thora neeche hai. Fourth quadrant: cos > 0, sin < 0.

Reference angle ki values
\[\cos 15^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.9659\]
\[\sin 15^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.2588\]
Kyun: \(15^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}\), aur \(\cos(A - B)\), \(\sin(A - B)\) ke formulas se yeh exact values milti hain. Exact values rakhne se jawab exact rehta hai; decimal sirf aakhir mein.

cos aur sin (sign ke saath)
\[\cos 345^{\circ} = \cos 15^{\circ} \approx 0.9659\]
\[\sin 345^{\circ} = -\sin 15^{\circ} \approx -0.2588\]
Kyun: fourth quadrant ke signs lagaye: cos plus, sin minus.

r se zarb dein
\[x = \dfrac{7(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2})}{4} \approx 6.76\]
\[y = -\dfrac{7(\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2})}{4} \approx -1.81\]
Kyun: \(7 \times 0.9659 = 6.761\) aur \(7 \times 0.2588 = 1.812\).

Tasdeeq (check):
\[6.761^{2} + 1.812^{2} \approx 49.0\]
is liye \(|z| \approx 7\). Real part positive aur imaginary negative, yani fourth quadrant. Sahi. (Answer key ka \(-6.47 - 2.17i\) third quadrant mein hai aur us ka modulus bhi 7 nahi, is liye woh ghalat hai.)
blocks.final_answer: \(z = \frac{7(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2})}{4} - \frac{7(\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2})}{4}i \approx 6.76 - 1.81i\): positive x-axis se thora neeche, O se 7 units door.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(-6.47 - 2.17i\) deti hai. Is ka real part ka sign ghalat hai (\(345^{\circ}\) fourth quadrant mein hai jahan cos positive hota hai) aur is ka modulus taqreeban 6.82 hai, 7 nahin. Sahi jawab \(6.76 - 1.81i\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iv) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(|z| = 11,\ \arg(z) = -\frac{11\pi}{12}\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Is baar angle negative hai, yani hum clockwise ghoomenge.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r = 11\), \(\theta = -\frac{11\pi}{12}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): z ko \(x + iy\) (rectangular form) mein likhna.
Method (tareeqa): \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\). Yeh is liye lagta hai ke cos 'daayein-baayein' ka hissa aur sin 'upar-neeche' ka hissa deta hai.

Angle badlein aur quadrant pehchanein
\[-\dfrac{11\pi}{12} = -11 \times 15^{\circ} = -165^{\circ}\]
\(165^{\circ}\) clockwise ghoomne se hum teesre (third) quadrant mein pohanchte hain; reference angle \(180^{\circ} - 165^{\circ} = 15^{\circ}\).
Kyun: clockwise \(90^{\circ}\) par negative y-axis aata hai aur \(180^{\circ}\) par negative x-axis; \(165^{\circ}\) in dono ke darmiyan hai, yani third quadrant. Wahan cos aur sin dono negative.

cos aur sin ki values
\[\cos(-165^{\circ}) = -\cos 15^{\circ} \approx -0.9659\]
\[\sin(-165^{\circ}) = -\sin 15^{\circ} \approx -0.2588\]
Kyun: size \(15^{\circ}\) se (exact values \(\frac{\sqrt{6} \pm \sqrt{2}}{4}\)), sign quadrant se.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) hota hai, is liye kuch students cos ko positive likh dete hain. Lekin \(\cos 165^{\circ}\) khud negative hai, is liye \(\cos(-165^{\circ})\) bhi negative hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[10.625^{2} + 2.847^{2} \approx 121.0\]
is liye \(|z| \approx 11\). Sahi. (Answer key ka \(-10.69\) sirf rounding ki chhoti ghalti hai; sahi \(-10.63\) hai.)
blocks.final_answer: \(z = -\frac{11(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2})}{4} - \frac{11(\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2})}{4}i \approx -10.63 - 2.85i\): third quadrant mein, negative x-axis ke thora neeche.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(-10.69 - 2.85i\) deti hai. Real part \(-11\cos 15^{\circ} \approx -10.625\) hai, is liye sahi jawab \(-10.63 - 2.85i\) hai (key mein rounding ki chhoti si ghalti).

blocks.prompt: 3 (v) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(|z| = \frac{10}{3},\ \arg(z) = -\frac{17\pi}{12}\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Yahan angle \(-255^{\circ}\) banta hai; is ko poora chakkar jama kar ke aasaan angle mein badlenge.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r = \frac{10}{3}\), \(\theta = -\frac{17\pi}{12}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): z ko \(x + iy\) (rectangular form) mein likhna.
Method (tareeqa): \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\). Yeh is liye lagta hai ke cos 'daayein-baayein' ka hissa aur sin 'upar-neeche' ka hissa deta hai.

Angle ko aasaan banayein
\[-\dfrac{17\pi}{12} = -17 \times 15^{\circ} = -255^{\circ}\]
\[-255^{\circ} + 360^{\circ} = 105^{\circ}\]
Kyun: \(360^{\circ}\) (poora chakkar) jama karne se cos aur sin nahi badalte, kyunke hum ghoom kar usi ray par aa jaate hain. \(105^{\circ}\) doosre (second) quadrant mein hai, reference angle \(180^{\circ} - 105^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}\).
Dhyan dein: \(-255^{\circ}\) ko dekh kar foran third ya fourth quadrant na samjhein; \(255^{\circ}\) clockwise jaane se hum second quadrant mein pohanchte hain.

cos aur sin ki values
\[\cos 105^{\circ} = -\cos 75^{\circ} = -\sin 15^{\circ}\]
\[\cos 105^{\circ} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx -0.2588\]
\[\sin 105^{\circ} = \sin 75^{\circ} = \cos 15^{\circ}\]
\[\sin 105^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4} \approx 0.9659\]
Kyun: second quadrant mein cos negative aur sin positive. Aur \(\cos 75^{\circ} = \sin 15^{\circ}\) is liye ke \(75^{\circ} + 15^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}\) (complementary angles ka cos doosre ka sin hota hai).

r se zarb dein
\[x = -\dfrac{10}{3}(0.2588) \approx -0.86\]
\[y = \dfrac{10}{3}(0.9659) \approx 3.22\]
Kyun: \(\frac{10}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{4} = \frac{10}{12} = \frac{5}{6}\), is liye exact jawab mein \(\frac{5}{6}\) aata hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[0.8627^{2} + 3.2198^{2} \approx 11.11\]
aur \(\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)^{2} = \frac{100}{9} \approx 11.11\). Sahi. (Answer key ke jawab ka modulus 3.75 hai, \(\frac{10}{3}\) nahi, is liye woh ghalat hai.)
blocks.final_answer: \(z = -\frac{5(\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2})}{6} + \frac{5(\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2})}{6}i \approx -0.86 + 3.22i\): second quadrant mein, positive y-axis ke thora baayein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(-2.43 + 2.86i\) deti hai. Is ka modulus taqreeban 3.75 hai, \(\frac{10}{3} \approx 3.33\) nahin. Sahi jawab \(-0.86 + 3.22i\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (vi) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(2\cos(-33) + i\,2\sin(-33)\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Is part mein kitab ne angle ke saath degree ka nishan nahi lagaya, is liye pehle yeh tay karna hai ke angle degrees mein hai ya radians mein.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = 2\cos(-33) + i\,2\sin(-33)\), yani \(r = 2\) aur \(\theta = -33\).
To find (maloom karna hai): \(x + iy\).
Method (tareeqa): pehle angle ki unit tay karein, phir \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\).

Angle ki unit tay karein
Kitab ne \(-33\) bina degree ke nishan ke likha hai. Is sawal ke baqi sab angles \(\pi\) ki shakal mein hain, aur answer key ka jawab \(1.68 - 1.09i\) degrees se banta hai, is liye hum ise \(-33^{\circ}\) parhte hain.
Kyun: agar \(-33\) radians hota to \(2\cos(-33) \approx -0.03\) aur \(2\sin(-33) \approx -2.00\) aate, jo key se nahi milte. Asool: jab angle ke saath \(\pi\) ya degree ka nishan na ho to aam taur par radians samjha jata hai, is liye yahan kitab ki printing ki ghalti hai.
Dhyan dein: calculator ka mode (DEG ya RAD) zaroor check karein; ghalat mode mein bilkul alag jawab aata hai.

cos aur sin ki values
\[\cos(-33^{\circ}) = \cos 33^{\circ} \approx 0.8387\]
\[\sin(-33^{\circ}) = -\sin 33^{\circ} \approx -0.5446\]
Kyun: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) (cos negative angle par sign nahi badalta) aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\). \(-33^{\circ}\) fourth quadrant mein hai. \(33^{\circ}\) standard angle nahi, is liye calculator use kiya.

r se zarb dein
\[x = 2(0.8387) \approx 1.68\]
\[y = 2(-0.5446) \approx -1.09\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\), r = 2 se zarb.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[1.6773^{2} + 1.0893^{2} \approx 4.00\]
is liye \(|z| = 2\). Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(z \approx 1.68 - 1.09i\) (angle ko \(-33^{\circ}\) parh kar): fourth quadrant mein, O se 2 units door.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab \(2\cos(-33) + i\,2\sin(-33)\) bina degree ke nishan ke chhaapti hai. Asal angle \(-33^{\circ}\) hai (answer key ka \(1.68 - 1.09i\) degrees se banta hai), is liye ise \(2\cos(-33^{\circ}) + i\,2\sin(-33^{\circ})\) parhein.

blocks.prompt: 3 (vii) Convert the complex number z into the rectangular form \(x + iy\): \(|z| = 12,\ \arg(z) = \pi\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh Sawal 2 ka ulta kaam hai: yahan humein r (faasla) aur \(\theta\) (direction) diye gaye hain, aur point ka 'address' x aur y mein likhna hai, yani \(x + iy\). Formula seedha hai: \(x = r\cos\theta\) aur \(y = r\sin\theta\). Asal mehnat angle par hai: plan yeh hai ke (1) angle ko degrees mein badal kar aasaan banayein (poore chakkar hata kar), (2) quadrant dekh kar cos aur sin ke sign tay karein, (3) reference angle se un ki values lein, (4) r se zarb dein, aur aakhir mein modulus check karein. Yeh sab se aasaan part hai: \(\pi\) seedha negative x-axis ki direction hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(r = 12\), \(\theta = \pi\).
To find (maloom karna hai): z ko \(x + iy\) (rectangular form) mein likhna.
Method (tareeqa): \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\). Yeh is liye lagta hai ke cos 'daayein-baayein' ka hissa aur sin 'upar-neeche' ka hissa deta hai.

cos aur sin ki values
\[\cos\pi = -1, \quad \sin\pi = 0\]
Kyun: \(\pi = 180^{\circ}\) ka matlab hai polar axis se aadha chakkar, yani bilkul ulti taraf, negative x-axis par. Wahan point ka 'daayein' hissa \(-1\) aur 'upar' hissa 0 hota hai.

r se zarb dein
\[z = 12(-1) + 12(0)i = -12 + 0i\]
Kyun: \(x = r\cos\theta = -12\), \(y = r\sin\theta = 0\).

Tasdeeq (check):
\(|-12| = 12\), aur \(-12\) negative real axis par hai jahan angle \(\pi\) hota hai. Sahi.
Kyun: is se yeh bhi samajh aata hai ke har negative real number ka argument \(\pi\) hota hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z = -12 + 0i\), yani sirf real number \(-12\), jo negative real axis par hai.
